sections.The line texts (Legge):
2 → 7. The Receptive → The Army.
Line: The second SIX, divided, (shows the attribute of) being straight, square, and great. (Its operation), without repeated efforts, will be in every respect advantageous.
Small Image: The movement indicated by the second six, (divided),is 'from the straight (line) to the square.' '(Its operation), without repeated effort, in every way advantageous,' shows the brilliant result of the way of earth.

3 → 60. Difficulty at the Beginning → Limitation.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows (its subject) distressed and obliged to return; (even) the horses of her chariot (also) seem to be retreating. (But) not by a spoiler (is she assailed), but by one who seeks her to be his wife. The young lady maintains her firm correctness, and declines a union. After ten years she will be united, and have children.
Small Image: The difficulty (to the subject of) the second six, (divided), arises from, its place over the undivided line below it. 'The union and children after ten years' shows things resuming their regular course.

8 → 29. Holding Together [Union] → The Abysmal (Water).
Line: In the second SIX, divided, we see the movement towards union and attachment proceeding from the inward (mind). With firm correctness there will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'The movement towards union and attachment proceeds from the inward (mind):'—(the party concerned) does not fail in what is proper to himself

12 → 6. Standstill [Stagnation] → Conflict.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject patient and obedient. To the small man (comporting himself so) there will be good fortune. If the great man (comport himself) as the distress and obstruction require, he will have success.
Small Image: 'The great man, comporting himself as the distress and obstruction require, will have success:—'he does not allow himself to be disordered by the herd (of small men).

13 → 1. Fellowship with Men → The Creative.
Line: The second SIX, divided, (shows the representative of) the union of men in relation with his kindred. There will be occasion for regret.
Small Image: '(The representative of) the union of men appears in relation with his kindred:'—that is the path to regret.

15 → 46. Modesty → Pushing Upward.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows us humility that has made itself recognised. With firm correctness there will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'The good fortune consequent on being firm and correct, where the humility has made itself recognised, is owing to the possessor's having (the virtue) in the core of his heart.

16 → 40. Enthusiasm → Deliverance.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows one who is firm as a rock. (He sees a thing) without waiting till it has come to pass; with his firm correctness there will be good fortune.
Small Image: '(He sees a thing) without waiting till it has come to pass; with his firm correctness there will be good fortune:'—this is shown by the central and correct position (of the line).

17 → 58. Following → The Joyous, Lake.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows us one who cleaves to the little boy, and lets go the man of age and experience.
Small Image: 'He cleaves to the little boy:'—he cannot be with the two at the same time.

20 → 59. Contemplation [View] → Dispersion [Dissolution].
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows one peeping out from a door. It would be advantageous if it were (merely) the firm correctness of a female.
Small Image: 'The firm correctness of a woman, in peeping out from a door' is also a thing to be ashamed of (in a superior man).

21 → 38. Biting Through → Opposition.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows one biting through the soft flesh, and (going on to) bite off the nose. There will be no error.
Small Image: 'He bites through the soft flesh, and (goes on) to bite off the nose:'—(the subject of the line) is mounted on the strong (first line).

22 → 26. Grace → The Taming Power of the Great.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows one adorning his beard.
Small Image: 'He adorns his beard:'—he rouses himself to action (only) along with the (subject of the) line above.

23 → 4. Splitting Apart → Youthful Folly.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows one overthrowing the couch by injuring its frame. (The injury will go on to) the destruction of (all) firm correctness, and there will be evil.
Small Image: 'He destroys the couch by injuring its frame:'—(the superior man) has as yet no associates.

24 → 19. Return (The Turning Point) → Approach.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows the admirable return (of its subject). There will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'The good fortune attendant on the admirable return (of the subject of the second line)' is due to his condescension to the virtuous (subject of the line) below.

25 → 10. Innocence (The Unexpected) → Treading [Conduct].
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows one who reaps without having ploughed (that he might reap), and gathers the produce of his third year's fields without having cultivated them the first year for that end. To such a one there will be advantage in whatever direction he may move.
Small Image: 'He reaps without having ploughed:'—(the thought of) riches to be got had not risen (in his mind).

27 → 41. The Corners of the Mouth (Providing Nourishment) → Decrease.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows one looking downwards for nourishment, which is contrary to what is proper; or seeking it from the height (above), advance towards which will lead to evil.
Small Image: 'The evil of advance by the subject of the second SIX, (divided),' is owing to his leaving in his movements his proper associates.

30 → 14. The Clinging, Fire → Possession in Great Measure.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject in his place in yellow. There will be great good fortune.
Small Image: 'The great good fortune (from the subject of the second line) occupying his place in yellow' is owing to his holding the course of the due mean.

31 → 28. Influence (Wooing) → Preponderance of the Great.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows one moving the calves of his leg. There will be evil. If he abide (quiet in his place), there will be good fortune.
Small Image: Though 'there would be evil; yet, if he abide (quiet) in his place, there will be good fortune:'—through compliance (with the circumstances of his condition and place) there will be no injury.

33 → 44. Retreat → Coming to Meet.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject holding (his purpose) fast as if by a (thong made from the) hide of a yellow ox, which cannot be broken.
Small Image: 'He holds it as; by (a thong from the hide of) a yellow ox:'—his purpose is firm.

35 → 64. Progress → Before Completion.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject with the appearance of advancing, and yet of being sorrowful. If he be firm and correct, there will be good fortune. He will receive this great blessing from his grandmother.
Small Image: 'He will receive this great blessing:'—for he is in the central place and the correct position for him.

36 → 11. Darkening of the Light → Peace.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject, (in the condition indicated by) Ming Î, wounded in the left thigh. He saves himself by the strength of a (swift) horse; and is fortunate.
Small Image: 'The good fortune of (the subject of) the second SIX, divided,' is due to the proper fashion of his acting according to his circumstances.

37 → 9. The Family [The Clan] → The Taming Power of the Small.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject taking nothing on herself, but in her central place attending to the preparation of the food. Through her firm correctness there will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'The good fortune attached to the second six, (divided),' is due to the docility (of its subject), operating with humility.

39 → 48. Obstruction → The Well.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows the minister of the king struggling with difficulty on difficulty, and not with a view to his own advantage.
Small Image: 'The minister of the king struggles with difficulty on difficulty:'—in the end no blame will be attached to him.

42 → 61. Increase → Inner Truth.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows parties adding to the stores of its subject ten pairs of tortoise shells whose oracles cannot be opposed. Let him persevere in being firm and correct, and there will be good fortune. Let the king, (having the virtues thus distinguished), employ them in presenting his offerings to God, and there will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'Parties add to his stores:'—they come from beyond (his immediate circle) to do so.

45 → 47. Gathering Together [Massing] → Oppression (Exhaustion).
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject led forward (by his correlate). There will be good fortune, and freedom from error. There is entire sincerity, and in that case (even the small offerings of) the vernal sacrifice are acceptable.
Small Image: 'He is led forward; there will be good fortune, and freedom from error:'—(the virtue proper to) his central place has not undergone any change.

49 → 43. Revolution (Molting) → Break-through (Resoluteness).
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject making his changes after some time has passed. Action taken will be fortunate. There will be no error.
Small Image: 'He makes his changes when some time has passed:'—what he does will be matter of admiration.

51 → 54. The Arousing (Shock, Thunder) → The Marrying Maiden.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject, when the movement approaches, in a position of peril. He judges it better to let go the articles (in his possession), and to ascend a very lofty height. There is no occasion for him to pursue after (the things he has let go); in seven days he will find them.
Small Image: 'When the movement approaches, he is in a position of peril:'—(a weak line) is mounted on a strong (one).

52 → 18. Keeping Still, Mountain → Work on what has been spoiled [Decay].
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject keeping the calves of his legs at rest. He cannot help (the subject of the line above) whom he follows, and is dissatisfied in his mind.
Small Image: 'He cannot help him whom he follows:'(he whom he follows) will not retreat to listen to him.

53 → 57. Development (Gradual Progress) → The Gentle (The Penetrating, Wind).
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows the geese gradually approaching the large rocks, where they eat and drink joyfully and at ease. There will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'They eat and drink joyfully and at ease:'—but not without having earned their food.

55 → 34. Abundance → The Power of the Great.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject surrounded by screens so large and thick that at midday he can see from them the constellation of the Bushel. If he go (and try to enlighten his ruler who is thus emblemed), he will make himself to be viewed with suspicion and dislike. Let him cherish his feeling of sincere devotion that he may thereby move (his ruler's mind), and there will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'Let him cherish his feeling of sincere devotion, that it shall appear being put forth:'—it is by sincerity that the mind is affected.

56 → 50. The Wanderer → The Caldron.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows the stranger, occupying his lodging-house, carrying with him his means of livelihood, and provided with good and trusty servants.
Small Image: 'He is provided with good and trusty servants:'—he will in the end have nothing of which to complain.

62 → 32. Preponderance of the Small → Duration.
Line: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject passing by his grandfather, and meeting with his grandmother; not attempting anything against his ruler, but meeting him as his minister. There will be no error.
Small Image: 'He does not attempt to reach his ruler:'—a minister should not overpass the distance (between his ruler and himself).

63 → 5. After Completion → Waiting (Nourishment).
Line: The second SIX, divided, (shows its subject as) a wife who has lost her (carriage-)screen. There is no occasion to go in pursuit of it. In seven days she will find it.
Small Image: 'In seven days she will find it:'—for the course pursued is that indicated by the central position (of the line).

sections.The line texts (Legge):
1 → 10. The Creative → Treading [Conduct].
Line: In the third NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as) the superior man active and vigilant all the day, and in the evening still careful and apprehensive. (The position is) dangerous, but there will be no mistake.
Small Image: 'Active and vigilant all the day:'—(this refers to) the treading of the (proper) path over and over again.

5 → 60. Waiting (Nourishment) → Limitation.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject in the mud (close by the stream). He thereby invites the approach of injury.
Small Image: 'He is waiting in the mud:'—calamity is (close at hand, and as it were) in the outer (trigram). 'He himself invites the approach of injury:'—if he be reverent and careful, he will not be worsted.

9 → 61. The Taming Power of the Small → Inner Truth.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, suggests the idea of a carriage, the strap beneath which has been removed, or of a husband and wife looking on each other with averted eyes.
Small Image: 'Husband and wife look on each other with averted eyes:'—(the subject of line three is like a husband who) cannot maintain correctly his relations with his wife.

11 → 19. Peace → Approach.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows that, while there is no state of peace that is not liable to be disturbed, and no departure (of evil men) so that they shall not return, yet when one is firm and correct, as he realises the distresses that may arise, he will commit no error. There is no occasion for sadness at the certainty (of such recurring changes); and in this mood the happiness (of the present) may be (long) enjoyed.
Small Image: 'There is no going away so that there shall not be a return' refers to this as the point where the interaction of heaven and earth takes place.

13 → 25. Fellowship with Men → Innocence (The Unexpected).
Line: The third NINE, undivided, (shows its subject) with his arms hidden in the thick grass, and at the top of a high mound. (But) for three years he makes no demonstration.
Small Image: 'He hides his arms in the thick grass:'—because of the strength of his opponent. 'For three years he makes no demonstration:'—how can he do anything?

14 → 38. Possession in Great Measure → Opposition.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows us a feudal prince presenting his offerings to the Son of Heaven. A small man would be unequal (to such a duty).
Small Image: 'A feudal prince presents his offerings to the son of Heaven:'—a small man (in such a position) does (himself) harm.

15 → 2. Modesty → The Receptive.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows the superior man of (acknowledged) merit. He will maintain his success to the end, and have good fortune.
Small Image: 'The superior man of (acknowledged) merit, and yet humble:'—the myriads of the people will submit to him.

18 → 4. Work on what has been spoiled [Decay] → Youthful Folly.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows (a son) dealing with the troubles caused by his father. There may be some small occasion for repentance, but there will not be any great error.
Small Image: 'He deals with the troubles caused by his father:'—in the end there will be no error.

22 → 27. Grace → The Corners of the Mouth (Providing Nourishment).
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject with the appearance of being adorned and bedewed (with rich favours). But let him ever maintain his firm correctness, and there will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'The good fortune consequent on his ever maintaining firm correctness' is due to this,—that to the end no one will insult him.

26 → 41. The Taming Power of the Great → Decrease.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject urging his way with good horses. It will be advantageous for him to realise the difficulty (of his course), and to be firm and correct, exercising himself daily in his charioteering and methods of defence; then there will be advantage in whatever direction he may advance.
Small Image: 'There will be advantage in whatever direction he may advance:'—(the subject of) the topmost line is of the same mind with him.

28 → 47. Preponderance of the Great → Oppression (Exhaustion).
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows a beam that is weak. There will be evil.
Small Image: 'The evil connected with the beam that is weak' arises from this, that no help can be given (to the condition thus represented).

30 → 21. The Clinging, Fire → Biting Through.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject in a position like that of the declining sun. Instead of playing on his instrument of earthenware, and singing to it, he utters the groans of an old man of eighty. There will be evil.
Small Image: 'A position like that of the declining sun:'—how can it continue long?

31 → 45. Influence (Wooing) → Gathering Together [Massing].
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows one moving his thighs, and keeping close hold of those whom he follows. Going forward (in this way) will cause regret.
Small Image: 'He moves his thighs:'—he still does not (want to) rest in his place. His will is set on 'following others:'—what he holds in his grasp is low.

32 → 40. Duration → Deliverance.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows one who does not continuously maintain his virtue. There are those who will impute this to him as a disgrace. However firm he may be, there will be ground for regret.
Small Image: 'He does not continuously maintain his virtue:'—nowhere will he be borne with.

33 → 12. Retreat → Standstill [Stagnation].
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows one retiring but bound,—to his distress and peril. (If he were to deal with his binders as in) nourishing a servant or concubine, it would be fortunate for him.
Small Image: 'The peril connected with the case of one retiring, though bound,' is due to the (consequent) distress and exhaustion. 'If he were (to deal as in) nourishing a servant or concubine, it would be fortunate for him:'—but a great affair cannot be dealt with in this way.

34 → 54. The Power of the Great → The Marrying Maiden.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows, in the case of a small man, one using all his strength; and in the case of a superior man, one whose rule is not to do so. Even with firm correctness the position would be perilous. (The exercise of strength in it might be compared to the case of) a ram butting against a fence, and getting his horns entangled.
Small Image: 'The small man uses all his strength; in the case of the superior man it is his rule not to do so.'

36 → 24. Darkening of the Light → Return (The Turning Point).
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject, (in the condition indicated by) Ming Î, hunting in the south, and taking the great chief (of the darkness). He should not be eager to make (all) correct (at once).
Small Image: With the aim represented by 'hunting in the south' a great achievement is accomplished.

37 → 42. The Family [The Clan] → Increase.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject (treating) the members of the household with stern severity. There will be occasion for repentance, there will be peril, (but) there will (also) be good fortune. If the wife and children were to be smirking and chattering, in the end there would be occasion for regret.
Small Image: When 'the members of the household are treated with stern severity,' there has been no (great) failure (in the regulation of the family). When 'wife and children are smirking and chattering,' the (proper) economy of the family has been lost.

39 → 8. Obstruction → Holding Together [Union].
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject advancing, (but only) to (greater) difficulties. He remains stationary, and returns (to his former associates).
Small Image: 'He advances, (but only) to (greater) difficulty; he remains stationary, and returns to his former associates:'—they, (represented in) the inner (trigram), rejoice in him.

43 → 58. Break-through (Resoluteness) → The Joyous, Lake.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject (about to advance) with strong (and determined) looks. There will be evil. (But) the superior man, bent on cutting off (the criminal), will walk alone and encounter the rain, (till he be hated by his proper associates) as if he were contaminated (by the others). (In the end) there will be no blame against him.
Small Image: 'The superior man looks bent on cutting off the culprit:'—there will in the end be no error.

44 → 6. Coming to Meet → Conflict.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows one from whose buttocks the skin has been stripped so that he walks with difficulty. The position is perilous, but there will be no great error.
Small Image: 'He walks with difficulty:'—but his steps have not yet been drawn (into the course of the first line).

46 → 7. Pushing Upward → The Army.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject ascending upwards (as into) an empty city.
Small Image: 'He advances upwards (as into) an empty city:'—he has no doubt or hesitation.

48 → 29. The Well → The Abysmal (Water).
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows a well, which has been cleared out, but is not used. Our hearts are sorry for this, for the water might be drawn out and used. If the king were (only) intelligent, both he and we might receive the benefit of it.
Small Image: 'The well has been cleared out, but is not used:'—(even) passers-by would be sorry for this. A prayer is made 'that the king were intelligent:'—for then blessing would be received.

49 → 17. Revolution (Molting) → Following.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows that action taken by its subject will be evil. Though he be firm and correct, his position is perilous. If the change (he contemplates) have been three times fully discussed, he will be believed in.
Small Image: 'The change (contemplated) has been three times fully discussed:'—to what else should attention (now) be directed?

50 → 64. The Caldron → Before Completion.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows the caldron with (the places of) its ears changed. The progress (of its subject) is (thus) stopped. The fat flesh of the pheasant (which is in the caldron) will not be eaten. But the (genial) rain will come, and the grounds for repentance will disappear. There will be good fortune in the end.
Small Image: 'There is the caldron with (the places for) its ears changed:'—(its subject) has failed in what was required of him (in his situation).

52 → 23. Keeping Still, Mountain → Splitting Apart.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject keeping his loins at rest, and separating the ribs (from the body below). The situation is perilous, and the heart glows with suppressed excitement.
Small Image: 'He keeps the loins at rest:'—the danger (from his doing so) produces a glowing, heat in the heart.

53 → 20. Development (Gradual Progress) → Contemplation [View].
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows them gradually advanced to the dry plains. (It suggests also the idea of) a husband who goes on an expedition from which he does not return, and of a wife who is pregnant, but will not nourish her child. There will be evil. (The case symbolised) might be advantageous in resisting plunderers.
Small Image: 'A husband goes and does not return:'—he separates himself from his comrades. 'A wife is pregnant, but will not nourish her child:'—she has failed in her (proper) course. 'It might be advantageous in resisting plunderers:'—by acting as here indicated men would preserve one another.

55 → 51. Abundance → The Arousing (Shock, Thunder).
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject with an (additional) screen of a large and thick banner, through which at midday he can see (the small) Mei star. (In the darkness) he breaks his right arm; but there will be no error.
Small Image: 'There is an (additional) screen of a large and thick banner:'—great things should not be attempted (in such circumstances). 'He breaks his right arm:'—in the end he will not be fit to be employed.

56 → 35. The Wanderer → Progress.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows the stranger, burning his lodging-house, and having lost his servants. However firm and correct he (try to) be, he will be in peril.
Small Image: 'The stranger burns his lodging-house:'—and he himself also suffers hurt thereby. When, as a stranger, he treats those below him (as the line indicates), the right relation between him and them is lost.

57 → 59. The Gentle (The Penetrating, Wind) → Dispersion [Dissolution].
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject penetrating (only) by violent and repeated efforts. There will be occasion for regret.
Small Image: 'The regret arising from the violent and repeated efforts to penetrate' shows the exhaustion of the will.

62 → 16. Preponderance of the Small → Enthusiasm.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject taking no extraordinary precautions against danger; and some in consequence finding opportunity to assail and injure him. There will be evil.
Small Image: 'Some in consequence find opportunity to assail and injure him. There will be evil:'—how great will it be!

63 → 3. After Completion → Difficulty at the Beginning.
Line: The third NINE, undivided, (suggests the case of) Kâo Žung, who attacked the Demon region, but was three years in subduing it. Small men should not be employed (in such enterprises).
Small Image: 'He was three years in subduing it:'—enough to make him weary.

sections.The line texts (Legge):
2 → 15. The Receptive → Modesty.
Line: The third SIX, divided, (shows its subject) keeping his excellence under restraint, but firmly maintaining it. If he should have occasion to engage in the king's service, though he will not claim the success (for himself), he will bring affairs to a good issue.
Small Image: 'He keeps his excellence under restraint, but firmly maintains it:'—at the proper time he will manifest it. 'He may have occasion to engage in the king's service:—great is the glory of his wisdom.

3 → 63. Difficulty at the Beginning → After Completion.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows one following the deer without (the guidance of) the forester, and only finding himself in the midst of the forest. The superior man, acquainted with the secret risks, thinks it better to give up the chase. If he went forward, he would regret it.
Small Image: 'One pursues the deer without the (guidance of the) forester:'—(he does so) in (his eagerness to) follow the game. 'The superior man gives up the chase, (knowing that) if he go forward he will regret it:'—he would be reduced to extremity.

4 → 18. Youthful Folly → Work on what has been spoiled [Decay].
Line: The third SIX, divided, (seems to say) that one should not marry a woman whose emblem it might be, for that, when she sees a man of wealth, she will not keep her person from him, and in no wise will advantage come from her.
Small Image: 'A woman (such as is here represented) should not be taken in marriage:'—her conduct is not agreeable to what is right.

6 → 44. Conflict → Coming to Meet.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject keeping in the old place assigned for his support, and firmly correct. Perilous as the position is, there will be good fortune in the end. Should he perchance engage in the king's business, he will not (claim the merit of) achievement.
Small Image: 'He confines himself to the support assigned to him of old:'—(thus) following those above him, he will have good fortune.

7 → 46. The Army → Pushing Upward.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows how the host may, possibly, have many inefficient leaders. There will be evil.
Small Image: 'The host with the possibility of its having many idle leaders:'—great will be its want of success.

8 → 39. Holding Together [Union] → Obstruction.
Line: In the third SIX, divided, we see its subject seeking for union with such as ought not to be associated with.
Small Image: 'Union is sought with such as ought not to be associated with:'—but will not injury be the result?

10 → 1. Treading [Conduct] → The Creative.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows a one-eyed man (who thinks he) can see; a lame man (who thinks he) can walk well; one who treads on the tail of a tiger and is bitten. (All this indicates) ill fortune. We have a (mere) bravo acting the part of a great ruler.
Small Image: 'A one-eyed man (who thinks that he) can see:'—he is not fit to see clearly. 'A lame man (who thinks that he can) tread well:'—one cannot walk along with him. 'The ill fortune of being bitten' arises from the place not being the proper one for him. 'A (mere) bravo acting the part of a great ruler:'—this is owing to his aims being (too) violent.

12 → 33. Standstill [Stagnation] → Retreat.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject ashamed of the purpose folded (in his breast).
Small Image: That 'his shame is folded in his breast' is owing to the inappropriateness of his position.

16 → 62. Enthusiasm → Preponderance of the Small.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows one looking up (for favours), while he indulges the feeling of pleasure and satisfaction. If he would understand!—If he be late in doing so, there will indeed be occasion for repentance.
Small Image: 'He looks up (for favours), while he indulges the feeling of satisfaction; there will be occasion for repentance:'—this is intimated by the position not being the appropriate one.

17 → 49. Following → Revolution (Molting).
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows us one who cleaves to the man of age and experience, and lets go the little boy. Such following will get what it seeks; but it will be advantageous to adhere to what is firm and correct.
Small Image: 'He cleaves to the man of age and experience:'—by the decision of his will, he abandons (the youth) below.

19 → 11. Approach → Peace.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows one well pleased (indeed) to advance, (but whose action) will be in no way advantageous. If he become anxious about it (however), there will be no error.
Small Image: 'He (shows himself) well pleased to advance:'—his position is not that appropriate to him. 'If he become anxious, however, about his action,' his error will not be continued.

20 → 53. Contemplation [View] → Development (Gradual Progress).
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows one looking at (the course of) his own life, to advance or recede (accordingly).
Small Image: 'He looks at (the course of his own life, to advance or recede (accordingly):'—he will not err in the path (to be pursued).

21 → 30. Biting Through → The Clinging, Fire.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows one gnawing dried flesh, and meeting with what is disagreeable. There will be occasion for some small regret, but no (great) error.
Small Image: 'He meets with what is disagreeable and hurtful:'—his position is not the proper one for him.

23 → 52. Splitting Apart → Keeping Still, Mountain.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject among the overthrowers; but there will be no error.
Small Image: That 'there will be no error on the part of this one among the overthrowers' arises from the difference between him and the others above and below.

24 → 36. Return (The Turning Point) → Darkening of the Light.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows one who has made repeated returns. The position is perilous, but there will be no error.
Small Image: Notwithstanding 'the perilous position of him who has made many returns,' there will be no error through (his aiming after righteousness).

25 → 13. Innocence (The Unexpected) → Fellowship with Men.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows calamity happening to one who is free from insincerity;—as in the case of an ox that has been tied up. A passer by finds it (and carries it off), while the people in the neighbourhood have the calamity (of being accused and apprehended).
Small Image: 'The passer-by gets the ox:'—this proves a calamity to the people of the neighbourhood.

27 → 22. The Corners of the Mouth (Providing Nourishment) → Grace.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows one acting contrary to the method of nourishing. However firm he may be, there will be evil. For ten years let him not take any action, (for) it will not be in any way advantageous.
Small Image: 'For ten years let him not take any action:'—his course is greatly opposed (to what is right).

29 → 48. The Abysmal (Water) → The Well.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject, whether he comes or goes (descends or ascends), confronted by a defile. All is peril to him and unrest. (His endeavours) will lead him into the cavern of the pit. There should be no action (in such a case).
Small Image: 'Whether he comes or goes, he is confronted by a defile:'—he will never (in such circumstances) achieve any success.

35 → 56. Progress → The Wanderer.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject trusted by all (around him). All occasion for repentance will disappear.
Small Image: 'All (around) trust him:'—their (common) aim is to move upwards and act.

38 → 14. Opposition → Possession in Great Measure.
Line: In the third SIX, divided, we see one whose carriage is dragged back, while the oxen in it are pushed back, and he is himself subjected to the shaving of his head and the cutting off of his nose. There is no good beginning, but there will be a good end.
Small Image: 'We see his carriage dragged back:'—this is indicated by the inappropriateness of the position (of the line). 'There is no (good) beginning, but there will be a (good) end:'—this arises from his meeting with the strong (subject of the topmost line).

40 → 32. Deliverance → Duration.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows a porter with his burden, (yet) riding in a carriage. He will (only) tempt robbers to attack him. However firm and correct he may (try to) be, there will be cause for regret.
Small Image: For 'a porter with his burden to be riding in a carriage' is a thing to be ashamed of. 'It is he himself that tempts the robbers to come:'—on whom besides can we lay the blame?

41 → 26. Decrease → The Taming Power of the Great.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows how of three men walking together, the number is diminished by one; and how one, walking, finds his friend.
Small Image: 'One man, walking,' (finds his friend):—when three are together, doubts rise among them.

42 → 37. Increase → The Family [The Clan].
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows increase given to its subject by means of what is evil, so that he shall (be led to good), and be without blame. Let him be sincere and pursue the path of the Mean, (so shall he secure the recognition of the ruler, like) an officer who announces himself to his prince by the symbol of his rank.
Small Image: 'Increase is given by means of what is evil and difficult:'—as he has in himself (the qualities called forth).

45 → 31. Gathering Together [Massing] → Influence (Wooing).
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject striving after union and seeming to sigh, yet nowhere finding any advantage. If he go forward, he will not err, though there may be some small cause for regret.
Small Image: 'If he go forward, he will not err:'—in the subject of the topmost line there is humility and condescension.

47 → 28. Oppression (Exhaustion) → Preponderance of the Great.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject straitened before a (frowning) rock. He lays hold of thorns. He enters his palace, and does not see his wife. There will be evil.
Small Image: 'He lays hold of thorns:'—(this is suggested by the position of the line) above the strong (line). 'He enters his palace, and does not see his wife:'—this is inauspicious.

51 → 55. The Arousing (Shock, Thunder) → Abundance.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject distraught amid the startling movements going on. If those movements excite him to (right) action, there will be no mistake.
Small Image: 'He is distraught amid the startling movements going on:'—(the third line) is in a position unsuitable to it.

54 → 34. The Marrying Maiden → The Power of the Great.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows the younger sister who was to be married off in a mean position. She returns and accepts an ancillary position.
Small Image: 'The younger sister who was to be married off is in a mean position:'—this is shown by the improprieties (indicated in the line).

58 → 43. The Joyous, Lake → Break-through (Resoluteness).
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject bringing round himself whatever can give pleasure. There will be evil.
Small Image: 'The evil predicated of one's bringing around himself whatever can give pleasure' is shown by the inappropriateness of the place (of the line).

59 → 57. Dispersion [Dissolution] → The Gentle (The Penetrating, Wind).
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject discarding any regard to his own person. There will be no occasion for repentance.
Small Image: 'He has no regard to his own person:'—his aim is directed to what is external to himself.

60 → 5. Limitation → Waiting (Nourishment).
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject with no appearance of observing the (proper) regulations, in which case we shall see him lamenting. But there will be no one to blame (but himself).
Small Image: In 'the lamentation for not observing the (proper) regulations,' who should there be to blame?

61 → 9. Inner Truth → The Taming Power of the Small.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject having met with his mate. Now he beats his drum, and now he leaves off. Now he weeps, and now he sings.
Small Image: 'Now he beats his drum, and now he leaves off:'—the position (of the line) is the appropriate one for it.

64 → 50. Before Completion → The Caldron.
Line: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject, with (the state of things) not yet remedied, advancing on; which will lead to evil. But there will be advantage in (trying to) cross the great stream.
Small Image: '(The state of things is) not yet remedied. Advancing will lead to evil:'—the place (of the line) is not that appropriate for it.

sections.The line texts (Legge):
1 → 9. The Creative → The Taming Power of the Small.
Line: In the fourth NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as the dragon looking) as if he were leaping up, but still in the deep. There will be no mistake.
Small Image: 'He seems to be leaping up, but is still in the deep:'—if he advance, there will be no error.

6 → 59. Conflict → Dispersion [Dissolution].
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject unequal to the contention. He returns to (the study of Heaven's) ordinances, changes (his wish to contend), and rests in being firm and correct. There will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'He returns to (the study of Heaven's) ordinances, changes (his wish to contend), and rests in being firm and correct:'—he does not fail (in doing what is right).

10 → 61. Treading [Conduct] → Inner Truth.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject treading on the tail of a tiger. He becomes full of apprehensive caution, and in the end there will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'He becomes full of apprehensive caution, and in the end there will be good fortune:'—his aim takes effect.

12 → 20. Standstill [Stagnation] → Contemplation [View].
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject acting in accordance with the ordination (of Heaven), and committing no error. His companions will come and share in his happiness.
Small Image: 'He acts in accordance with the ordination (of Heaven), and commits no error:'—the purpose of his mind can be carried into effect.

13 → 37. Fellowship with Men → The Family [The Clan].
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, (shows its subject) mounted on the city wall; but he does not proceed to make the attack (he contemplates). There will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'He is mounted on his city-wall;' but yielding to the right, 'he does not proceed to make the attack (he contemplated).' (Where it is said),'There will be good fortune,' (that shows how) he feels the strait he is in, and returns to the rule of law.

14 → 26. Possession in Great Measure → The Taming Power of the Great.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject keeping his great resources under restraint. There will be no error.
Small Image: 'He keeps his great resources under restraint:'—his wisdom discriminates clearly (what he ought to do).

16 → 2. Enthusiasm → The Receptive.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows him from whom the harmony and satisfaction come. Great is the success which he obtains. Let him not allow suspicions to enter his mind, and thus friends will gather around him.
Small Image: 'From him the harmony and satisfaction come; great is the success which he obtains:'—his aims take effect on a grand scale.

17 → 3. Following → Difficulty at the Beginning.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows us one followed and obtaining (adherents). Though he be firm and correct, there will be evil. If he be sincere (however) in his course, and make that evident, into what error will he fall?
Small Image: 'He is followed and obtains adherents:'—according to the idea (of the hexagram), this is evil. 'He is sincere in his course:'—showing his intelligence, and leading to achievement.

21 → 27. Biting Through → The Corners of the Mouth (Providing Nourishment).
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows one gnawing the flesh dried on the bone, and getting the pledges of money and arrows. It will be advantageous to him to realise the difficulty of his task and be firm,—in which case there will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'It will be advantageous to him to realise the difficulty of his task and be firm, in which case there will be good fortune:'—his light has not yet been sufficiently displayed.

25 → 42. Innocence (The Unexpected) → Increase.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows (a case) in which, if its subject can remain firm and correct, there will be no error.
Small Image: 'If he can remain firm and correct there will be no error:'—he firmly holds fast (his correctness).

28 → 48. Preponderance of the Great → The Well.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows a beam curving upwards. There will be good fortune. If (the subject of it) looks for other (help but that of line one), there will be cause for regret.
Small Image: 'The good fortune connected with the beam curving upwards' arises from this, that it does not bend towards what is below.

30 → 22. The Clinging, Fire → Grace.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows the manner of its subject's coming. How abrupt it is, as with fire, with death, to be rejected (by all)!
Small Image: 'How abrupt is the manner of his coming!'—none can bear with him.

31 → 39. Influence (Wooing) → Obstruction.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows that firm correctness which will lead to good fortune, and prevent all occasion for repentance. If its subject be unsettled in his movements, only his friends will follow his purpose.
Small Image: 'Firm correctness will lead to good fortune, and prevent all occasion for repentance:'—there has not yet been any harm from (a selfish wish to) influence. 'He is unsettled in his movements:'(his power to influence) is not yet either brilliant or great.

32 → 46. Duration → Pushing Upward.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows a field where there is no game.
Small Image: (Going) for long to what is not his proper place, how can he get game?

33 → 53. Retreat → Development (Gradual Progress).
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject retiring notwithstanding his likings. In a superior man this will lead to good fortune; a small man cannot attain to this.
Small Image: 'A superior man retires notwithstanding his likings; a small man cannot attain to this.'

34 → 11. The Power of the Great → Peace.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows (a case in which) firm correctness leads to good fortune, and occasion for repentance disappears. (We see) the fence opened without the horns being entangled. The strength is like that in the wheel‐spokes of a large waggon.
Small Image: 'The fence is opened and the horns are not entangled:'—(the subject of the line) still advances.

35 → 23. Progress → Splitting Apart.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject with the appearance of advancing, but like a marmot. However firm and correct he may be, the position is one of peril.
Small Image: '(He advances like) a marmot. However firm and correct he may be, his position is one of peril:'—his place is not that appropriate for him.

38 → 41. Opposition → Decrease.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject solitary amidst the (prevailing) disunion. (But) he meets with the good man (represented by the first line), and they blend their sincere desires together. The position is one of peril, but there will be no mistake.
Small Image: 'They blend their sincere desires together, and there will be no error:'—their (common) aim is carried into effect.

40 → 7. Deliverance → The Army.
Line: (To the subject of) the fourth NINE, undivided, (it is said), 'Remove your toes. Friends will (then) come, between you and whom there will be mutual confidence.'
Small Image: 'Remove your toes:'—the places (of this line and of the third and first) are all inappropriate to them.

43 → 5. Break-through (Resoluteness) → Waiting (Nourishment).
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows one from whose buttocks the skin has been stripped, and who walks slowly and with difficulty. (If he could act) like a sheep led (after its companions), occasion for repentance would disappear. But though he hear these words, he will not believe them.
Small Image: 'He walks slowly and with difficulty:'—he is not in the place appropriate to him. 'He hears these words, but does not believe them:'—he hears, but does not understand.

44 → 57. Coming to Meet → The Gentle (The Penetrating, Wind).
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject with his wallet, but no fish in it. This will give rise to evil.
Small Image: 'The evil' indicated by there being 'no fish in the wallet' is owing to (the subject of the line) keeping himself aloof from the people.

45 → 8. Gathering Together [Massing] → Holding Together [Union].
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject in such a state that, if he be greatly fortunate, he will receive no blame.
Small Image: 'If he be grandly fortunate, he will receive no blame:'—(this condition is necessary, because) his position is not the one proper to him.

47 → 29. Oppression (Exhaustion) → The Abysmal (Water).
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject proceeding very slowly (to help the subject of the first line), who is straitened by the carriage adorned with metal in front of him. There will be occasion for regret, but the end will be good.
Small Image: 'He proceeds very slowly (to help the subject of the first line):'—his aim is directed to (help) that lower (line). Although he is not in his appropriate place, he and that other will (in the end) be together.

49 → 63. Revolution (Molting) → After Completion.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows occasion for repentance disappearing (from its subject). Let him be believed in; and though he change (existing) ordinances, there will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'The good fortune consequent on changing (existing) ordinances' is due to the faith reposed in his aims.

50 → 18. The Caldron → Work on what has been spoiled [Decay].
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows the caldron with its feet broken; and its contents, designed for the ruler's use, overturned and spilt. Its Subject will be made to blush for shame. There will be evil.
Small Image: 'The contents designed for the ruler's use are overturned and spilt:'—how can (the subject of the line) be trusted?

51 → 24. The Arousing (Shock, Thunder) → Return (The Turning Point).
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject, amid the startling movements, supinely sinking (deeper) in the mud.
Small Image: 'Amid the startling movements, he sinks supinely in the mud:'—the light in him has not yet been brilliantly developed.

54 → 19. The Marrying Maiden → Approach.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows the younger sister who is to be married off protracting the time. She may be late in being married, but the time will come.
Small Image: (The purpose in) 'protracting the time' is that, after waiting, the thing may be done (all the better).

55 → 36. Abundance → Darkening of the Light.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject in a tent so large and thick that at midday he can see from it the constellation of the Bushel. But he meets with the subject of the (first) line, undivided like himself. There will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'He is surrounded by a screen large and thick:'—the position of the line is inappropriate. 'At midday he sees the constellation of the Bushel:'—there is darkness and no light. 'He meets with the subject of the line, undivided like himself. There will be good fortune:'—action may be taken.

56 → 52. The Wanderer → Keeping Still, Mountain.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows the traveller in a resting-place, having (also) the means of livelihood and the axe, (but still saying), 'I am not at ease in my mind.'
Small Image: 'The stranger is in a resting-place:'—but he has not got his proper position. 'He has the means of livelihood, and the axe:'—but his mind is not at ease.

58 → 60. The Joyous, Lake → Limitation.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject deliberating about what to seek his pleasure in, and not at rest. He borders on what would be injurious, but there will be cause for joy.
Small Image: 'The joy in connexion with (the subject of) the fourth NINE, (undivided): is due to the happiness (which he will produce).

62 → 15. Preponderance of the Small → Modesty.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject falling into no error, but meeting (the exigency of his situation), without exceeding (in his natural course). If he go forward, there will be peril, and he must be cautious. There is no occasion to be using firmness perpetually.
Small Image: 'He meets the exigency (of his situation), without exceeding (the proper course):'—(he does so), the position being inappropriate (for a strong line). 'If he go forward, there will be peril, and he must be cautious:'—the result would be that his course would not be long pursued.

64 → 4. Before Completion → Youthful Folly.
Line: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject by firm correctness obtaining good fortune, so that all occasion for repentance disappears. Let him stir himself up, as if he were invading the Demon region, where for three years rewards will come to him (and his troops) from the great kingdom.
Small Image: (By firm correctness there is good fortune, and cause for repentance disappears:'—the aim (of the subject of the line) is carried into effect.

sections.The line texts (Legge):
2 → 16. The Receptive → Enthusiasm.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, (shows the symbol of) a sack tied up. There will be no ground for blame or for praise.
Small Image: 'A sack tied up;—there will be no error:'—this shows how, through carefulness, no injury will be received.

3 → 17. Difficulty at the Beginning → Following.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows (its subject as a lady), the horses of whose chariot appear in retreat. She seeks, however, (the help of) him who seeks her to be his wife. Advance will be fortunate; all will turn out advantageously.
Small Image: 'Going forward after such a search (for a helper)' shows intelligence.

4 → 64. Youthful Folly → Before Completion.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, (shows its subject as if) bound in chains of ignorance. There will be occasion for regret.
Small Image: 'The regret arising from ignorance bound in chains' is due to the special distance of (the subject of this line) from the solidity (shown in lines 2 and 6).

5 → 43. Waiting (Nourishment) → Break-through (Resoluteness).
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject waiting in (the place of) blood. But he will get out of the cavern.
Small Image: 'He is waiting in (the place of) blood:'—he accommodates himself (to the circumstances of the time), and hearkens to (its requirements).

7 → 40. The Army → Deliverance.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows the host in retreat. There is no error.
Small Image: 'The host is in retreat; but there is no error:'—there has been no failure in the regular course.

8 → 45. Holding Together [Union] → Gathering Together [Massing].
Line: In the fourth SIX, divided, we see its subject seeking for union with the one beyond himself. With firm correctness there will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'Union is sought (by the party intended here) with one beyond himself, and (in this case) with a worthy object:'—he is following (the ruler) above him.

9 → 1. The Taming Power of the Small → The Creative.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject possessed of sincerity. The danger of bloodshed is thereby averted, and his (ground for) apprehension dismissed. There will be no mistake.
Small Image: 'He is possessed of sincerity; his (ground for) apprehension is dismissed:'—(the subjects of the lines) above agree in aim with him.

11 → 34. Peace → The Power of the Great.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject fluttering (down);—not relying on his own rich resources, but calling in his neighbours. (They all come) not as having received warning, but in the sincerity (of their hearts).
Small Image: 'He comes fluttering (down), not relying on his own rich resources:'—both he and his neighbours are out of their real (place where they are). 'They have not received warning, but (come) in the sincerity (of their hearts):'—this is what they have desired in the core of their hearts.

15 → 62. Modesty → Preponderance of the Small.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one, whose action would be in every way advantageous, stirring up (the more) his humility.
Small Image: 'One, whose action would be in every way advantageous, stirs up his humility the more:'(but in doing so) he does not act contrary to the (proper) rule.

18 → 50. Work on what has been spoiled [Decay] → The Caldron.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows (a son) viewing indulgently the troubles caused by his father. If he go forward, he will find cause to regret it.
Small Image: 'He views indulgently the troubles caused by his father:'—if he go forward, he will not succeed.

19 → 54. Approach → The Marrying Maiden.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one advancing in the highest mode. There will be no error.
Small Image: 'The freedom from error consequent on the advance in the highest mode' is due to the (various) appropriateness of the position.

20 → 12. Contemplation [View] → Standstill [Stagnation].
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one contemplating the glory of the kingdom. It will be advantageous for him, being such as he is, (to seek) to be a guest of the king.
Small Image: 'He contemplates the glory of the kingdom:'(thence) arises the wish to be a guest (at court).

22 → 30. Grace → The Clinging, Fire.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one looking as if adorned, but only in white. As if (mounted on) a white horse, and furnished with wings, (he seeks union with the subject of the first line), while (the intervening third pursues), not as a robber, but intent on a matrimonial alliance.
Small Image: 'The place occupied by the fourth six, (divided),' affords ground for doubt (as to its subject); but '(as the subject of the third pursues) not as a robber, but as intent on a matrimonial alliance,' he will in the end have no grudge against him.

23 → 35. Splitting Apart → Progress.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject having overthrown the couch, and (going to injure) the skin (of him who lies on it). There will be evil.
Small Image: 'He has overthrown the couch, and (proceeds to injure) the skin (of him who lies on it):'—calamity is very near at hand.

24 → 51. Return (The Turning Point) → The Arousing (Shock, Thunder).
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject moving right in the centre (among those represented by the other divided lines), and yet returning alone (to his proper path).
Small Image: 'He moves right in the centre (among those represented by the other divided lines), and yet returns alone:'—his object is to pursue the (proper) path.

26 → 14. The Taming Power of the Great → Possession in Great Measure.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows the young bull, (and yet) having the piece of wood over his horns. There will be great good fortune.
Small Image: 'The great good fortune indicated by the fourth six, (divided),' shows that there is occasion for joy.

27 → 21. The Corners of the Mouth (Providing Nourishment) → Biting Through.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one looking downwards for (the power to) nourish. There will be good fortune. Looking with a tiger's downward unwavering glare, and with his desire that impels him to spring after spring, he will fall into no error.
Small Image: 'The good fortune attached to looking downwards for (the power to) nourish,' shows how brilliant will be the diffusion (of that power) from (the subject of the line's) superior position.

29 → 47. The Abysmal (Water) → Oppression (Exhaustion).
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject (at a feast), with (simply) a bottle of spirits, and a subsidiary basket of rice, while (the cups and bowls) are (only) of earthenware. He introduces his important lessons (as his ruler's) intelligence admits. There will in the end be no error.
Small Image: '(Nothing but) a bottle of spirits and a subsidiary basket of rice:'—(these describe) the meeting at this point of (those who are represented by) the strong and weak lines.

36 → 55. Darkening of the Light → Abundance.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject (just) entered into the left side of the belly (of the dark land). (But) he is able to carry out the mind appropriate (in the condition indicated by) Ming Î, quitting the gate and courtyard (of the lord of darkness).
Small Image: 'He has (just) entered into the left side of the belly (of the dark land):'—he is still able to carry out the idea in his (inner) mind.

37 → 13. The Family [The Clan] → Fellowship with Men.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject enriching the family. There will be great good fortune.
Small Image: 'The family is enriched, and there is great good fortune:'—this is due to the docility (belonging to the subject of the line), and its being in its correct place.

39 → 31. Obstruction → Influence (Wooing).
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject advancing, (but only) to (greater) difficulties. He remains stationary, and unites (with the subject of the line above).
Small Image: 'To advance will (only be to) encounter (greater) difficulties; he remains stationary, and unites (with the subject of the line above):'—that is in its proper place and has the solidity (due to it in that position).

41 → 38. Decrease → Opposition.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject diminishing the ailment under which he labours by making (the subject of the first line) hasten (to his help), and make him glad. There will be no error.
Small Image: 'He diminishes the ailment under which he labours:'—this is matter for joy.

42 → 25. Increase → Innocence (The Unexpected).
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject pursuing the due course. His advice to his prince is followed. He can with advantage be relied on in such a movement as that of removing the capital.
Small Image: 'His advice to his prince is followed:'—his (only) object in it being the increase (of the general good).

46 → 32. Pushing Upward → Duration.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject employed by the king to present his offerings on mount Khî. There will be good fortune; there will be no mistake.
Small Image: 'The king employs him to prevent his offerings on mount Khi:'—such a service (of spiritual Beings) is according to (their mind).

48 → 28. The Well → Preponderance of the Great.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows a well, the lining of which is well laid. There will be no error.
Small Image: 'A well the lining of which is well laid. There will be no error:'—the well has been put in good repair.

52 → 56. Keeping Still, Mountain → The Wanderer.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject keeping his trunk at rest. There will be no error.
Small Image: 'He keeps the trunk of his body at rest:'—he keeps himself free (from agitation).

53 → 33. Development (Gradual Progress) → Retreat.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows the geese gradually advanced to the trees. They may light on the flat branches. There will be no error.
Small Image: 'They may light on the flat branches:'—there is docility (in the line) going on to flexible penetration.

57 → 44. The Gentle (The Penetrating, Wind) → Coming to Meet.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows all occasion for repentance (in its subject) passed away. He takes game for its threefold use in his hunting.
Small Image: 'He takes game in his hunting, enough for the threefold use of it:'—he achieves merit.

59 → 6. Dispersion [Dissolution] → Conflict.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject scattering the (different) parties (in the state); which leads to great good fortune. From the dispersion (he collects again good men standing out, a crowd) like a mound, which is what ordinary men would not have thought of.
Small Image: 'He scatters the (different) parties (in the state), and there is great good fortune:'—brilliant and great (are his virtue and service).

60 → 58. Limitation → The Joyous, Lake.
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject quietly and naturally (attentive to all) regulations. There will be progress and success.
Small Image: 'The progress and success of the quiet and natural (attention) to all regulations' is due to the deference which accepts the ways of (the ruler) above.

61 → 10. Inner Truth → Treading [Conduct].
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject (like) the moon nearly full, and (like) a horse (in a chariot) whose fellow disappears. There will be no error.
Small Image: 'A horse the fellow of which disappears:'—he breaks from his (former) companions, and mounts upwards.

63 → 49. After Completion → Revolution (Molting).
Line: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject with rags provided against any leak (in his boat), and on his guard all day long.
Small Image: 'He is on his guard all the day:'—he is in doubt about something.

sections.The line texts (Legge):
1 → 43. The Creative → Break-through (Resoluteness).
Line: In the sixth (or topmost) NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as) the dragon exceeding the proper limits. There will be occasion for repentance.
Small Image: 'The dragon exceeds the proper limits;—there will be occasion for repentance:'—a state of fullness, that is, should not be indulged in long.

4 → 7. Youthful Folly → The Army.
Line: In the topmost NINE, undivided, we see one smiting the ignorant (youth). But no advantage will come from doing him an injury. Advantage would come from warding off injury from him.
Small Image: 'Advantage will come from warding off injury:'—(the subject of this line) above and (the ignorant) below, all do and are done to in accordance with their nature.

6 → 47. Conflict → Oppression (Exhaustion).
Line: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows how its subject may have the leathern belt conferred on him (by the sovereign), and thrice it shall be taken from him in a morning.
Small Image: 'He receives the robe through his contention:'—but still be is not deserving of respect.

9 → 5. The Taming Power of the Small → Waiting (Nourishment).
Line: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows how the rain has fallen, and the (onward progress) is stayed;—(so) must we value the full accumulation of the virtue (represented by the upper trigram). But a wife (exercising restraint), however firm and correct she may be, is in a position of peril, (and like) the moon approaching to the full. If the superior man prosecute his measures (in such circumstances), there will be evil.
Small Image: 'The rain has fallen and (the onward progress) is stayed:'—the power (denoted in the figure) has accumulated to the full. 'If the superior man prosecute his measures, there will be evil:'—he will find himself obstructed.

10 → 58. Treading [Conduct] → The Joyous, Lake.
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, tells us to look at (the whole course) that is trodden, and examine the presage which that gives. If it be complete and without failure, there will be great good fortune.
Small Image: 'There will be great good fortune,' and that in the occupancy of the topmost line:—this is great matter for congratulation.

12 → 45. Standstill [Stagnation] → Gathering Together [Massing].
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows the overthrow (and removal of) the condition of distress and obstruction. Before this there was that condition. Hereafter there will be joy.
Small Image: 'The distress and obstruction having reached its end, it is overthrown and removed:'—how could it be prolonged?

13 → 49. Fellowship with Men → Revolution (Molting).
Line: The topmost NINE, undivided, (shows the representative of) the union of men in the suburbs. There will be no occasion for repentance.
Small Image: '(The representative of) the union of men appears in the suburbs:'—his object has not yet been attained.

14 → 34. Possession in Great Measure → The Power of the Great.
Line: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject with help accorded to him from Heaven. There will be good fortune, advantage in every respect.
Small Image: 'The good fortune attached to the topmost line of Ta Yu' arises from the help of Heaven.

18 → 46. Work on what has been spoiled [Decay] → Pushing Upward.
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows us one who does not serve either king or feudal lord, but in a lofty spirit prefers (to attend to) his own affairs.
Small Image: 'He does not serve either king or feudal lord:'—but his aim may be a model (to others).

20 → 8. Contemplation [View] → Holding Together [Union].
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject contemplating his character to see if it be indeed that of a superior man. He will not fall into error.
Small Image: 'He contemplates his own character:'—he cannot even yet let his mind be at rest.

21 → 51. Biting Through → The Arousing (Shock, Thunder).
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows one wearing the cangue, and deprived of his ears. There will be evil.
Small Image: 'He wears the cangue and is deprived of his ears:'—he hears, but will not understand.

22 → 36. Grace → Darkening of the Light.
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows one with white as his (only) ornament. There will be no error.
Small Image: 'The freedom from error attached to (the subject of) the topmost line, with no ornament but the (simple white),' shows how he has attained his aim.

23 → 2. Splitting Apart → The Receptive.
Line: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject (as) a great fruit which has not been eaten. The superior man finds (the people again) as a chariot carrying him. The small men (by their course) overthrow their own dwellings.
Small Image: 'The superior man finds himself in a carriage:'—he is carried along by the people. 'The small men (by their course) overthrow their own dwellings:'—they can. never again be of use to them.

25 → 17. Innocence (The Unexpected) → Following.
Line: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject free from insincerity, yet sure to fall into error, if he take action. (His action) will not be advantageous in any way.
Small Image: 'The action (in this case) of one who is free from insincerity' will occasion the calamity arising from action (when the time for it is) exhausted.

26 → 11. The Taming Power of the Great → Peace.
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject (as) in command of the firmament of heaven. There will be progress.
Small Image: 'In command of the firmament of heaven:'—the way is grandly open for movement.

27 → 24. The Corners of the Mouth (Providing Nourishment) → Return (The Turning Point).
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows him from whom comes the nourishing. His position is perilous, but there will be good fortune. It will be advantageous to cross the great stream.
Small Image: 'The good fortune, notwithstanding the peril of his position, of him from whom comes the nourishing,' affords great cause for congratulation.

30 → 55. The Clinging, Fire → Abundance.
Line: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows the king employing its subject in his punitive expeditions. Achieving admirable (merit), he breaks (only) the chiefs (of the rebels). Where his prisoners were not their associates, he does not punish. There will be no error.
Small Image: 'The king employs him in his punitive expeditions:'—the object is to bring the regions to a correct state.

33 → 31. Retreat → Influence (Wooing).
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject retiring in a noble way. It will be advantageous in every respect.
Small Image: 'He retires in a noble way, and his doing so will be advantageous in every respect:'—he who does so has no doubts about his course.

35 → 16. Progress → Enthusiasm.
Line: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows one advancing his horns. But he only uses them to punish the (rebellious people of his own) city. The position is perilous, but there will be good fortune. (Yet) however firm and correct he may be, there will be occasion for regret.
Small Image: 'He uses his horns only to punish (the rebellious people of) his city:'—his course of procedure is not yet brilliant.

37 → 63. The Family [The Clan] → After Completion.
Line: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject possessed of sincerity and arrayed in majesty. In the end there will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'The good fortune connected with the display of majesty' describes (the result of) the recovery of the true character.

38 → 54. Opposition → The Marrying Maiden.
Line: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject solitary amidst the (prevailing) disunion. (In the subject of the third line, he seems to) see a pig bearing on its back a load of mud, (or fancies) there is a carriage full of ghosts. He first bends his bow against him, and afterwards unbends it, (for he discovers) that he is not an assailant to injure, but a near relative. Going forward, he shall meet with (genial) rain, and there will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'The good fortune symbolised by meeting with (genial) rain' springs from the passing away of all doubts.

41 → 19. Decrease → Approach.
Line: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject giving increase to others without taking from himself. There will be no error. With firm correctness there will be good fortune. There will be advantage in every movement that shall be made. He will find ministers more than can be counted by their clans.
Small Image: 'He gives increase to others without taking from what is his own:'—he obtains his wish on a grand scale.

42 → 3. Increase → Difficulty at the Beginning.
Line: In the sixth NINE, undivided, we see one to whose increase none will contribute, while many will seek to assail him. He observes no regular rule in the ordering of his heart. There will be evil.
Small Image: 'To his increase none will contribute:'—this expresses but half the result. 'Many will seek to assail him:'—they will come from beyond (his immediate circle) to do so.

44 → 28. Coming to Meet → Preponderance of the Great.
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject receiving others on his horns. There will be occasion for regret, but there will be no error.
Small Image: 'He receives others on his horns:'—he is exhausted at his greatest height, and there will be cause for regret.

50 → 32. The Caldron → Duration.
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows the caldron with rings of jade. There will be great good fortune, and all action taken will be in every way advantageous.
Small Image: 'The rings of jade' are at the very top:—the strong and the weak meet in their due proportions.

52 → 15. Keeping Still, Mountain → Modesty.
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject devotedly maintaining his restfulness. There will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'There is good fortune through his devotedly maintaining his restfulness:'—to the end he shows himself generous and good.

53 → 39. Development (Gradual Progress) → Obstruction.
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows the geese gradually advanced to the large heights (beyond). Their feathers can be used as ornaments. There will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'Their feathers can be used as ornaments. There will be good fortune:'—(the object and character of the subject of the line) cannot be disturbed.

56 → 62. The Wanderer → Preponderance of the Small.
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, suggests the idea of a bird burning its nest. The stranger, (thus represented), first laughs and then cries out. He has lost his ox(-like docility) too readily and easily. There will be evil.
Small Image: 'Considering that the stranger is here at the very height (of distinction),' with the spirit that possesses him, it is right he (should be emblemed by a bird) burning (its nest). 'He loses his ox(-like docility) too readily and easily:'—to the end he would not listen to (the truth about the course to be pursued).

57 → 48. The Gentle (The Penetrating, Wind) → The Well.
Line: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows the representative of penetration beneath a couch, and having lost the axe with which he executed his decisions. However firm and correct he may (try to) be, there will be evil.
Small Image: 'The representative of penetration is beneath a couch:'—though occupying the topmost place, his powers are exhausted. 'He has lost the axe with which he executed his decisions:'—though he try to be correct, there will be evil.

59 → 29. Dispersion [Dissolution] → The Abysmal (Water).
Line: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject disposing of (what may be called) its bloody wounds, and going and separating himself from its anxious fears. There will be no error.
Small Image: 'His bloody wounds are gone:'—he is far removed from the danger of injury.

61 → 60. Inner Truth → Limitation.
Line: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject in chanticleer (trying to) mount to heaven. Even with firm correctness there will be evil.
Small Image: 'Chanticleer (tries to) mount to heaven:'—but how can (such an effort) continue long?

64 → 40. Before Completion → Deliverance.
Line: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject full of confidence and therefore feasting (quietly). There will be no error. (If he) cherish this confidence, till he (is like the fox who) gets his head immersed, it will fail of what is right.
Small Image: 'He drinks and gets his head immersed:'—he does not know how to submit to the (proper) regulations.
