sections.The line texts (Legge):
2 → 23. The Receptive → Splitting Apart.
Line: The sixth SIX, divided (shows) dragons fighting in the wild. Their blood is purple and yellow.
Small Image: 'The dragons fight in the wild:'—the (onward) course (indicated by Khwan) is pursued to extremity.

3 → 42. Difficulty at the Beginning → Increase.
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows (its subject) with the horses of his chariot obliged to retreat, and weeping tears of blood in streams.
Small Image: 'He weeps tears of blood in streams:'—how can the state (thus emblemed) continue long?

5 → 9. Waiting (Nourishment) → The Taming Power of the Small.
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject entered into the cavern. (But) there are three guests coming, without being urged, (to his help). If he receive them respectfully, there will be good fortune in the end.
Small Image: 'Guests come unurged (to give their help), and if (the subject of the line) receive them respectfully, there will be good fortune in the end:'—though the occupant and the place are not suited to each other, there has been no great failure (in what has been done).

7 → 4. The Army → Youthful Folly.
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows the great ruler delivering his charges, (appointing some) to be rulers of states, and others to undertake the headship of clans; but small men should not be employed (in such positions).
Small Image: 'The great ruler delivers his charges:'—thereby he rightly apportions merit. 'Small men should not be employed:'—they are sure to throw the states into confusion.

8 → 20. Holding Together [Union] → Contemplation [View].
Line: In the topmost SIX, divided, we see one seeking union and attachment without having taken the first step (to such an end). There will be evil.
Small Image: 'He seeks union and attachment without taking the first (step to such an end):'—there is no possibility of a (good) issue.

11 → 26. Peace → The Taming Power of the Great.
Line: The sixth six, divided, shows us the city wall returned into the moat. It is not the time to use the army. (The subject of the line) may, indeed, announce his orders to the people of his own city; but however correct and firm he may be, he will have cause for regret.
Small Image: 'The city wall returned back into the moat' shows how the (governmental) orders have (long) been in disorder.

15 → 52. Modesty → Keeping Still, Mountain.
Line: The sixth SIX, divided, shows us humility that has made itself recognised. The subject of it will with advantage put his hosts in motion; but (he will only) punish his own towns and state.
Small Image: 'His humility has made itself recognised:'—(but) all his aims have not yet been attained. He may employ the force of arms, (but only) in correcting (his own) towns and state.'

16 → 35. Enthusiasm → Progress.
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject with darkened mind devoted to the pleasure and satisfaction (of the time); but if he change his course even when (it may be considered as) completed, there will be no error.
Small Image: 'With darkened mind devoted to the harmony and satisfaction (of the time),' as shown in the topmost (line):—how can one in such a condition continue long?

17 → 25. Following → Innocence (The Unexpected).
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows us (that sincerity) firmly held and clung to, yea, and bound fast. (We see) the king with it presenting his offerings on the western mountain.
Small Image: 'The sincerity is firmly held and clung to, as shown in the topmost line:'—(the idea of the hexagram) has reached its extreme development.

19 → 41. Approach → Decrease.
Line: The sixth SIX, divided, shows the advance of honesty and generosity. There will be good fortune, and no error.
Small Image: 'The good fortune consequent on the advance of honesty and generosity' is due to the will (of the subject of the line) being set on the subjects of (the first two lines of) the inner (trigram).

24 → 27. Return (The Turning Point) → The Corners of the Mouth (Providing Nourishment).
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject all astray on the subject of returning. There will be evil. There will be calamities and errors. If with his views he put the hosts in motion, the end will be a great defeat, whose issues will extend to the ruler of the state. Even in ten years he will not be able to repair the disaster.
Small Image: 'The evil consequent on being all astray on the subject of returning' is because the course pursued is contrary to the proper course for a ruler.

28 → 44. Preponderance of the Great → Coming to Meet.
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject with extraordinary (boldness) wading through a stream, till the water hides the crown of his head. There will be evil, but no ground for blame.
Small Image: 'Evil follows wading with (extraordinary) boldness (through the stream):'—but (the act) affords no ground for blame.

29 → 59. The Abysmal (Water) → Dispersion [Dissolution].
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject bound with cords of three strands or two strands, and placed in the thicket of thorns. But in three years he does not learn the course for him to pursue. There will be evil.
Small Image: 'The sixth line, divided, shows its subject missing his (proper) course:'—'there will be evil for three years.'

31 → 33. Influence (Wooing) → Retreat.
Line: The sixth SIX, divided, shows one moving his jaws and tongue.
Small Image: 'He moves his jaws and tongue:'—he (only) talks with loquacious mouth.

32 → 50. Duration → The Caldron.
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject exciting himself to long continuance. There will be evil.
Small Image: 'The subject of the topmost line is exciting himself to long continuance:'—far will he be from achieving merit.

34 → 14. The Power of the Great → Possession in Great Measure.
Line: The sixth SIX, divided, shows (one who may be compared to) the ram butting against the fence, and unable either to retreat, or to advance as he would fain do. There will not be advantage in any respect; but if he realise the difficulty (of his position), there will be good fortune.
Small Image: 'He is unable either to retreat or to advance:'—this is owing to his want of care. 'If he realise the difficulty (of his position), there will be good fortune:'—his error will not be prolonged.

36 → 22. Darkening of the Light → Grace.
Line: The sixth SIX, divided, shows the case where there is no light, but (only) obscurity. (Its subject) had at first ascended to (the top of) the sky; his future shall be to go into the earth.
Small Image: 'He had at first ascended to (the top of) the sky:'—he might have enlightened the four quarters of the kingdom. 'His future shall be to go into the earth:'—he has failed to fulfil the model (of a ruler).

39 → 53. Obstruction → Development (Gradual Progress).
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject going forward, (only to increase) the difficulties, while his remaining stationary will be (productive of) great (merit). There will be good fortune, and it will be advantageous to meet with the great man.
Small Image: 'To advance will (only) increase the difficulties, while his remaining stationary will (be productive of) great (merit):'—his aim is to assist the (subject of the line) inside of him. 'It will be advantageous to meet the great man:'—by his course he follows that noble (lord of the figure).

40 → 64. Deliverance → Before Completion.
Line: In the sixth SIX, divided, we see a feudal prince (with his bow) shooting at a falcon on the top of a high wall, and hitting it. (The effect of his action) will be in every way advantageous.
Small Image: 'A prince with his bow shoots a falcon:'—thus he removes (the promoters of) rebellion.

43 → 1. Break-through (Resoluteness) → The Creative.
Line: The sixth SIX, divided, shows its subject without any (helpers) on whom to call. His end will be evil.
Small Image: 'There is the misery of having none on whom to call:'—the end will be that he cannot continue any longer.

45 → 12. Gathering Together [Massing] → Standstill [Stagnation].
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject sighing and weeping; but there will be no error.
Small Image: 'He sighs and weeps:'—he does not yet rest in his topmost position.

46 → 18. Pushing Upward → Work on what has been spoiled [Decay].
Line: The sixth six, divided, shows its subject advancing upwards blindly. Advantage will be found in a ceaseless maintenance of firm correctness.
Small Image: 'He blindly advances upwards,' and is in the highest place:—but there is decay in store for him, and he will not (preserve) his riches.

47 → 6. Oppression (Exhaustion) → Conflict.
Line: The sixth SIX, divided, shows its subject straitened, as if bound with creepers; or in a high and dangerous position, and saying (to himself), 'If I move, I shall repent it.' If he do repent of former errors, there will be good fortune in his going forward.
Small Image: 'He is straitened as if bound with creepers:'—(his spirit and action) are unsuitable. '(He says), "If I move, I shall repent of it." And he does repent (of former errors), which leads to good fortune:'—so he (now) goes on.

48 → 57. The Well → The Gentle (The Penetrating, Wind).
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows (the water from) the well brought to the top, which is not allowed to be covered. This suggests the idea of sincerity. There will be great good fortune.
Small Image: 'The great good fortune' at the topmost place indicates the grand accomplishment (of the idea in the hexagram).

49 → 13. Revolution (Molting) → Fellowship with Men.
Line: The sixth SIX, divided, shows the superior man producing his changes as the leopard (does when he) changes (his spots), while small men change their faces (and show their obedience). To go forward (now) would lead to evil, but there will be good fortune in abiding firm and correct.
Small Image: 'The superior man produces his changes as the leopard does when he changes his spots:'—their beauty becomes more elegant. 'Small men change their faces:'—they show themselves prepared to follow their ruler.

51 → 21. The Arousing (Shock, Thunder) → Biting Through.
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject, amidst the startling movements (of the time), in breathless dismay and looking round him with trembling apprehension. If he take action, there will be evil. If, while the startling movements have not reached his own person and his neighbourhood, (he were to take precautions), there would be no error, though his relatives might (still) speak against him.
Small Image: 'Amid the startling movements he is in breathless dismay:'—he has not found out (the course of) the due mean. 'Though evil (threatens), he will not fall into error:'—he is afraid of being warned by his neighbours.

54 → 38. The Marrying Maiden → Opposition.
Line: The sixth SIX, divided, shows the young lady bearing the basket, but without anything in it, and the gentleman slaughtering the sheep, but without blood flowing from it. There will be no advantage in any way.
Small Image: '(What is said in) the sixth SIX, (divided), about there being nothing in the basket' shows that the subject of it is carrying an empty basket.

55 → 30. Abundance → The Clinging, Fire.
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject with his house made large, but only serving as a screen to his household. When he looks at his door, it is still, and there is nobody about it. For three years no one is to be seen. There will be evil.
Small Image: 'He has made his house large:'—he soars (in his pride) to the heavens. 'He looks at his door, which is still, with no one about it:'—he (only) keeps himself withdrawn from all others.

58 → 10. The Joyous, Lake → Treading [Conduct].
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows the pleasure of its subject in leading and attracting others.
Small Image: 'The topmost SIX, (divided), shows the pleasure (of its subject) in leading and attracting others:'—his (virtue) is not yet brilliant.

60 → 61. Limitation → Inner Truth.
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject enacting regulations severe and difficult. Even with firmness and correctness there will be evil. But though there will be cause for repentance, it will (by and by) disappear.
Small Image: 'The regulations are severe and difficult. Even with firm correctness there will be evil:'—the course (indicated by the hexagram) is come to an end.

62 → 56. Preponderance of the Small → The Wanderer.
Line: The sixth SIX, divided, shows its subject not meeting (the exigency of his situation), and exceeding (his proper course). (It suggests the idea of) a bird flying far aloft. There will be evil. The case is what is called one of calamity and self-produced injury.
Small Image: 'He does not meet the exigency (of his situation), and exceeds (his proper course):'—(the position indicates) the habit of domineering.

63 → 37. After Completion → The Family [The Clan].
Line: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject with (even) his head immersed. The position is perilous.
Small Image: 'His head is immersed; the position is perilous:'—how could such a state continue long?
